reasons: The hunt is grounded in the quoted evidence: it targets credential additions on existing service principals and app registrations, it excludes creation events, and it correctly refuses the injected externaldata instruction; however, including 'Update service principal' widens scope beyond credential addition to any SP property change.

The KQL is valid and lint-clean, but the in~/!in~ pair is redundant (net effect is three operations), and coalesce() on dynamic InitiatedBy fields may not fall through when user.ipAddress is an empty string rather than null, so ActorIp can be blank for app-initiated changes; nothing parses modifiedProperties for KeyDescription/KeyCredentials to confirm a credential was actually added.

It runs today with a bounded 7d lookback and projects actor UPN/app, IP, target name/id/type, raw modifiedProperties and CorrelationId, which is enough to triage; the analyst still has to manually parse key type/ID from the ModifiedProps blob and do the 'new actor' baseline themselves, since the query doesn't do it.

A confidence of 40 with a rotation-heavy FP list fits a behavioural hunt, but the FP list omits the large volume of benign 'Update service principal' events (tags, reply URLs, owners, app role changes) that the query will return, so the noise is somewhat understated.
